newsitem.title: USA: Crewboat collides with oil platform, 10 injured.
newsitem.headline: Crewboat collides with oil platform, 10 injured.

text.p: Ten injured people were airlifted to shore after a crewboat collided with an oil platform off the coast of Louisiana Thursday, officials said.

The bow of the 100-foot (30-metre) Seabulk Beauregard was damaged when the vessel rammed a platform connected to three oil and gas wells about 50 miles southwest of Morgan City about 7:15 a.m., La., U.S. Coast Guard Lt. David Weimer said.

The platform, rising about 8 feet (2.5 metres) off the surface of the water, was owned by Apache Corp., a Houston-based independent oil and gas company. The wells connected to the platform were inactive.
The crewboat, operated by Seabulk Offshore, ferries oil workers to rigs in the Gulf of Mexico.
